title: Functional analysis of sex-lethal (sxl ) gene in Dendroctonus armandi  Tsai et Li (Coleoptera: Curculionidae: Scolytinae) and its response to environmental treatment
content:
Abstract
Sex-determining genes act as core regulators of sexual differentiation in insects. The sex-lethal (sxl) gene plays a widely conserved central role in insect sex determination, but it had not been identified in Dendroctonus armandi until now. In this study, we cloned and functionally analyzed 4 alternatively spliced isoforms of the Dasxl gene, namely Dasxl1, Dasxl2, Dasxl3, and Dasxl4—using RNA interference (RNAi) technology. These 4 isoforms were expressed throughout all developmental stages, and their expression levels showed significant differences between adult males and females. Their expression was also influenced by temperature, feeding duration, and terpenoid exposure in a sexually dimorphic manner. RNAi experiments revealed complex regulatory interactions among the 4 isoforms, knocking down one isoform frequently led to substantial changes in the others. Furthermore, silencing individual Dasxl isoforms significantly increased mortality and reduced emergence rates in D. armandi. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for further research on the sex determination cascade in this species.
